minutes.summary: The Master Plan Steering Committee reviewed feedback-collection status from town boards on the draft plan, debated state 40Y/40R housing incentive programs and lake public-access feasibility, and discussed the town's hazard mitigation plan and planning-director hiring status. what_happened.line: Committee set an October 22 public info session and confirmed a November 18 special town meeting to present the master plan draft.
No funding votes were taken; the only recorded vote was to adjourn.
Members debated the state's 40Y/40R starter-home zoning incentive programs, which pay the town for zoning changes and per unit built, without giving dollar figures.
The committee weighed the feasibility of public access to Lake Shirley, including lifeguards, parking and ADA improvements, without costing it.
The committee will compile a master list of externally required plans, including hazard mitigation, to fold into the master plan.

why_it_matters: The master plan draft that residents will be asked about is now scheduled for a public Q&A on October 22 and a vote at the November 18 special town meeting.
The 40Y/40R programs discussed could change zoning to allow starter homes in exchange for state incentive payments, a decision that would need town approval.
Any move toward public lake access would likely require new staff and site work, which would show up as a future budget request rather than this meeting's business.
